issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch: docstring says max_steps/val_interval but code reads max_step and never uses val_interval
issues.detail: DeepSpeedTrainer.__init__ docstring lists trainer_args keys as max_steps, log_interval, val_interval, save_interval, but the implementation reads trainer_args['max_step'] (singular) and never references val_interval at all. log_interval is read but unused in practice. Validation cadence is wired to save_interval instead of val_interval. Any caller following the documented contract gets a KeyError; the documented val_interval semantics are silently absent. Pick one name, document it, and use it consistently.

issues.description: run()/train() termination is unenforced: global_step can overshoot max_step or fail to advance, spinning forever or saving past the bound
issues.detail: The outer 'while global_step < max_step' relies on train() advancing global_step by exactly save_interval, but there is no per-step max_step check inside train() and no progress assertion. If save_interval does not divide max_step, training overshoots by up to save_interval-1. If train()'s iterator yields zero batches (empty epoch, shard exhausted, state file drained), global_step never increments and the outer loop spins forever, repeatedly running valid() and writing duplicate checkpoints at the same step. State the invariant ('every outer iteration strictly advances global_step; final step <= max_step') and enforce it.

issues.description: Checkpoint cadence is broken: save fires unconditionally after every train() return rather than at multiples of save_interval
issues.detail: run() calls self.train() with iterator length=self.save_interval, then unconditionally saves a checkpoint after every train() return. There is no save_interval check, no per-step gating, and no guard against re-saving the same step. If train() exits early (data exhausted before save_interval steps), or save_interval does not divide max_step, the global_step encoded in the checkpoint directory name will not match the documented 'Steps between checkpoints' contract. The invariant 'a checkpoint exists at every multiple of save_interval and only there' is not maintained.

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats has fragile collective semantics, mutates caller state, and lies about it in the docstring
issues.detail: The function iterates `for key in stats` and issues per-key async all_reduce ops. Collectives require every rank to invoke the same op in the same order with the same shapes/dtypes/devices — none of which is asserted (only an isinstance(Tensor) check). Different stats keys across ranks (e.g. an optional metric emitted only when a batch contains a task type) will deadlock NCCL or corrupt. The function also mutates the caller's tensors in place (the model's returned stats dict), so `out['stats']` post-call holds rank-mean values rather than the model's original output — complecting value, identity, and time. The docstring claims 'modified in-place to contain averaged values' but the actual semantics differ between single-process (no division) and distributed (sum then divide) modes, which means the postcondition is non-uniform. Either pack stats into a single fixed-shape tensor and reduce once, or return a new dict and validate rank-consistency up front.

issues.description: _load_checkpoint silently falls back to latest-on-disk when an explicit --resume_path does not exist
issues.detail: The logic is: if resume_path and resume_path.exists() -> use it; elif checkpoints dir exists -> use latest. If the user passes --resume_path pointing at a typo'd or wrong-mount path, the code silently picks the latest checkpoint in output_dir, which is almost certainly not what the user intended. For long-running multi-team training, silently resuming the wrong run is a serious correctness hazard. The Optional[Path] representation cannot distinguish 'no request' from 'request that failed'. Raise on missing resume_path, or at minimum log loudly that fallback is occurring.

issues.description: _load_checkpoint may pass a leaf step_N directory directly to DeepSpeed's load_checkpoint, but the documented API expects parent dir + tag
issues.detail: model_engine.load_checkpoint(load_dir, tag=None) is DeepSpeed's documented interface; DeepSpeed scans load_dir for tag subdirectories. The code passes the step_N directory itself as load_dir without a tag. Either the author has verified by reading DeepSpeed source that this path works, or it doesn't — but no verification or comment is present. Combined with the sort key int(name.split('step_')[-1]) which throws on any non-conforming sibling directory, the resume path is under-specified.

issues.description: torch.cuda.set_device(args.local_rank) runs before validating that local_rank is set
issues.detail: args.local_rank has default=None. If the launcher does not pass --local_rank (older deepspeed launcher, debugging, env-var-only launchers like LOCAL_RANK), torch.cuda.set_device(None) raises an opaque TypeError before logging is configured, making the failure hard to diagnose. Read from env LOCAL_RANK as fallback, assert it is a non-negative int < device_count, and emit a clear error message if violated.

issues.description: Specifier parsing uses str.split() on whitespace for a colon-delimited format with no documentation of the multi-spec separator
issues.detail: args.valid_unregistered_specifier.split() and args.valid_registered_specifier.split() assume specifiers are whitespace-separated, but the help text only documents the per-spec format 'task:name:data_json[:factor]' and never mentions that multiple specs are whitespace-separated. A path containing a space (real in practice) will be silently misparsed; commas or other separators a user might naturally try will not work. Worse, the same code is not applied to train specifiers, which are passed as a single string — so the CLI surface is inconsistent between train and valid. Use nargs='+' or an explicit delimited form and apply uniformly.

issues.description: Checkpoint discovery uses fragile 'step_' substring match and integer parse with no validation
issues.detail: checkpoints = [d for d in ckpt_dir.iterdir() if d.is_dir() and 'step_' in d.name] then sorts by int(x.name.split('step_')[-1]). Any directory containing 'step_' anywhere is included; 'pre_step_warmup' matches, 'step_100_backup' is split to '100_backup' and crashes int(). The invariant 'checkpoint dir contains only step_<positive int> subdirs' is unstated and unenforced by the writer side. Use a regex anchored to '^step_(\d+)$', startswith plus try/except, or write a manifest/latest symlink so identity is explicit instead of name-parsed.

issues.description: Validation averaging weights each batch equally instead of by batch size, and can divide by zero on empty validation iterators
issues.detail: valid() accumulates per-batch scalar floats into lists and reports sum(values)/len(values). For variable-size batches (typical with length-bucketed batchfy), this is a batch-weighted mean rather than a sample-weighted mean — the reported 'val/<name>/loss' silently disagrees with what readers expect. Combined with the all_reduce-then-divide-by-world-size already applied per batch, the final number is a mean-of-batch-means-of-rank-means, not the true validation loss. If a validation factory yields zero batches (real risk under sharded loaders), len(value)==0 raises ZeroDivisionError. A single NaN in any batch silently poisons the metric. Switch to a (sum, count) running accumulator weighted by sample/token count, and decide an explicit NaN policy.

issues.description: wandb is a mandatory hidden dependency: the docstring asserts wandb.run must be non-None but no code check exists
issues.detail: The class docstring states 'IMPORTANT: wandb is MANDATORY... The trainer will raise an error if wandb.run is None,' but no such assertion exists in __init__. Instead the trainer calls wandb.config.update and wandb.log unconditionally, which fails with opaque attribute errors if the precondition is violated. wandb is also coupled directly into the trainer rather than behind a logger interface, which forces rank-1+ processes in train.py to initialize wandb in 'disabled' mode just to satisfy the contract. Either enforce the assertion the docstring promises, or accept a logger callback/sink list and keep wandb out of the trainer; the latter makes the trainer testable without wandb.

issues.description: freeze_param uses string-prefix matching on parameter names with no zero-match warning
issues.detail: Freezing logic is `k.startswith(t + '.') or k == t` over named_parameters(). This is a leaky abstraction over PyTorch's dotted-name convention, requires the caller to know the exact internal module path, and over-/under-matches sibling names depending on prefix punctuation. Worst of all, a typo silently matches zero parameters and training proceeds with nothing frozen — a classic source of 'why is my fine-tune not converging' bugs. Express against model.get_submodule()/named_modules() and assert >0 matches per pattern, or log the matched count.

issues.description: train_dtype: under 'amp' the function returns bf16/fp16 even though AMP/autocast expects fp32 inputs
issues.detail: When amp is enabled, the code returns bfloat16 or float16 and to_device casts inputs to that dtype. PyTorch AMP (and DeepSpeed's amp) manages dtype automatically via autocast and expects fp32 model inputs; casting inputs to fp16/bf16 upstream bypasses amp's semantics and may cause dtype-mismatch in ops that require fp32. The function conflates 'engine training dtype' with 'input cast dtype' — distinct properties — and the postcondition is not written down. Additionally the function derives dtype from the ds_config dict rather than asking the initialized engine (self.model_engine.bfloat16_enabled()/fp16_enabled()), creating two sources of truth that will drift. The function also does not use self and belongs as a module-level @staticmethod or free function for testability.

issues.description: main() lacks try/finally around distributed init and wandb teardown; a rank crash leaks resources and hangs siblings
issues.detail: deepspeed.init_distributed, model construction, dataloader construction, and trainer.run() can all raise. wandb.finish() is only reached on success, leaking offline runs on failure. No try/finally surrounds torch.distributed cleanup — a rank that crashes mid-training leaves siblings hanging at the next collective. Wrap main() in try/finally that tears down distributed cleanly and finishes wandb.

issues.description: DataIteratorFactory interface is inconsistent: train passes unregistered+registered specs positionally, valid passes them as kwargs one at a time
issues.detail: train_iterator_factory is constructed with two positional specifier strings; valid factories are built by looping over .split() and passing either unregistered_specifier= or registered_specifier= as a kwarg. The underlying constructor must accept both as optional kwargs but is invoked positionally on train, creating a position-sensitive, ambiguous contract. The valid_iterator_args dict shared across both loops via **kwargs further hides the construction-time facts (rank, world_size, stats_dir, collate_fn). Tighten the constructor signature to named kwargs only or a single specifiers list; promote shared loader config to a typed struct.

issues.description: Specifier strings 'task:name:data_json[:factor]' are an ad-hoc encoding of a structured value
issues.detail: A space-separated list of colon-separated 4-tuples is parsed at every entry point. The fields (task, name, json path, optional factor) are real data and deserve a real shape. A YAML/JSON list of {task, name, json, factor} entries in the train config eliminates the parsing layer entirely, removes the 'is the factor present' ambiguity, and avoids the silent path-with-space failures noted elsewhere. The string format is easy (one CLI flag) but not simple (a parser, a docstring, multiple entry-points to keep in sync).

issues.description: Tensor->float conversion via float(v.cpu()) requires scalar tensors, with no precondition check
issues.detail: float(v.cpu()) requires v to be 0-dim or 1-element. The precondition 'every value in stats[*] is a scalar tensor' is nowhere documented or checked. A model returning per-token or per-sample loss tensors crashes here, after _all_reduce_stats has already mutated state. The defensive isinstance(Tensor) check exists in the wrong place; the shape/scalar check that would actually help is absent.

issues.description: Non-rank-0 log level CRITICAL discards crash context from other ranks
issues.detail: Setting log_level='CRITICAL' on all non-zero ranks means when one rank crashes, debugging information is lost. At least leave WARNING on, or write per-rank log files to disk. Silence-by-default on stdout is fine; losing crash context is not.

issues.description: wandb.log uses step=self.global_step before global_step is incremented, causing duplicate step logs on resume
issues.detail: In train(), wandb.log(stats, step=self.global_step) runs before self.global_step += 1. On resume, the first logged step equals the resumed global_step, which is also the last step logged before the checkpoint was saved. wandb may emit warnings or drop the duplicate. Either log at step+1 ('completed step') or document that step indexes the step about to complete.

issues.description: Mixed kebab-case and snake_case CLI flag naming
issues.detail: Most flags use kebab (--train-config, --output-dir, --train-unregistered-specifier) but --local_rank and --resume_path use underscores. argparse normalizes both to underscore attrs, so the code works, but the user-facing CLI is inconsistent. Pick one convention (snake to match the launcher-imposed --local_rank, or kebab everywhere with --local_rank documented as a launcher exception).

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats lacks a literate comment explaining async-then-wait pattern and its preconditions
issues.detail: The function uses async_op=True, collects handles, waits, then divides by world_size — a real algorithmic choice the reader must reverse-engineer. A 2-line comment stating preconditions (identical key set across ranks, tensors on same device, sum semantics), rationale (overlap latency across keys), and postcondition (stats now holds rank-mean values) would make it readable without running.

issues.description: Redundant checkpoints dir exists() check after init guarantees it exists
issues.detail: __init__ does (self.output_dir / 'checkpoints').mkdir(exist_ok=True, parents=True), so the elif (self.output_dir / 'checkpoints').exists() branch in _load_checkpoint is always taken when resume_path is None. The list might be empty (correctly handled), but the .exists() check is dead. Remove for clarity.

issues.description: rank-aware log format frozen at config time will surprise future contributors adding dynamic context
issues.detail: log_format interpolates rank/world_size at config-time, not log-time. Fine here (rank doesn't change), but if someone later adds dynamic context (job_id, step), rebuilding basicConfig won't work. Consider a logging Filter that injects context per record.

issues.description: logger.info(f'...') eagerly formats strings even when the log level filters them out
issues.detail: Pre-formatted f-strings inside logger calls eliminate the deferred-evaluation benefit of the logging module. On rank>0 with level=CRITICAL it is harmless, but the pattern set here will be copied into per-batch hot paths. Prefer logger.info('%s', x).

issues.description: PR bundles three separable changes (launcher, trainer, wandb-mandatory policy) in one commit
issues.detail: The wandb-is-mandatory design choice is separable and would be easier to review and revert on its own. Not a blocker — next time, three patches.

issues.description: No tests in the diff; pure-Python pieces are testable
issues.detail: _load_checkpoint sorting, _all_reduce_stats tensor handling, and train_dtype branching are all pure-Python and testable without a GPU. New trainer + launcher shipping with zero tests is a regression in maintainability.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers independently converged on the same P0: the trainer_args contract is broken — docstring promises max_steps/val_interval, code reads max_step and never uses val_interval, so any caller following the documentation gets a KeyError and validation cadence is silently bound to save_interval. Five of six (Knuth, Hickey, Liskov, Pike, Dijkstra) also flag run()/train() termination as fundamentally unenforced: global_step can overshoot max_step by up to save_interval-1, or fail to advance at all on an empty iterator and spin forever rewriting the same checkpoint. Five flag _all_reduce_stats as dangerous on multiple axes (in-place mutation of caller state, no rank-consistency check on key set/order/dtype/device, non-uniform postcondition between single-process and distributed). The clearest preserved disagreement is on severity of the max_step overshoot and the resume_path silent-fallback: Hickey and Dijkstra escalate the loop-termination issue to P0 on structured-programming/complecting grounds, while Knuth/Liskov/Pike treat it as P1; Liskov uniquely escalates the resume_path fallback to P0 as a correctness hazard for multi-team runs, while Pike rates it P1 and four others do not flag it. Sub-themes flagged by multiple reviewers but with smaller spreads: validation averaging is batch-weighted not sample-weighted (six reviewers), checkpoint discovery via 'step_' substring is fragile (five), wandb is a mandatory hidden dependency whose precondition is asserted in prose but not code (four), and CLI naming mixes kebab/snake inconsistently (five). Dijkstra alone raises absence of try/finally around distributed cleanup and the AMP dtype-casting conflation as P0/P1 specification failures.
